Many cars were victim to turn 1 with spin-outs and rolls. This being our first experience with the short course, we learned a couple valuable lessons: let up around the turns when the track is freshly watered and make sure you have beadlock rings that can handle the higher tire pressures. One hard hit blew our rear beadlock ring clean off the car, putting us at the end of the pack and having to do the LCQ race. The LCQ lap is where we ended with our rollover.

videos.title: 1st Lap at Area BFE Moab, Ultra 4 #4401 | Epic 4x4 Quest and ORI Struts
videos.description:
Thanks to Epic 4x4 Quest and ORI Struts making this race in Moab happen! Without Nathan Livingston at Epic 4X4 Quest, and his exceptional racing knowledge, we wouldn't have pulled this race off. 

Check out their YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC0trHSTUXBVJBQFsem05o9w

Overall standing was 9th place. We are pretty happy, considering we had transfer case issues. First problem was user error, we should have been running a different gear ratio, so our low gear was too low for any speed and our high gear was too high, causing the transmission to over heat in this terrain. Also there were issues shifting. If you see us stop on course a couple times it was because of shifting issues. 

We also lost a tire, slowing us down significantly.

So we took it easy, held the car together and got a 9th place position. Not bad for being only our 3rd race ever.

videos.title: 2016 RZR XP Turbo EPS at 30mph Over Whoops At Five Mile Pass In Utah
videos.description: Testing out the durability of the Fox Shocks over some pretty aggressive whoops at 5-mile pass in Utah. Did several takes with the suspension on the softest setting. The faster I went the more the tracking was throne off and it would toss the back end from side to side. You can see it in the video pretty clearly at some points.

videos.title: Stock Polaris RZR XP Turbo EPS Test Drive | Jensen Brothers
videos.description: Took the RZR out to the Little Sahara Sand Dunes in Utah for a test drive. We ran the Fox Shocks at 6 notches down from the hardest setting. So about mid range softness. It handles the whoops great but there was some side to side movement and bucking of the rear end when going over jumps. Power slides and hard turns are scary because it was diving into the turns. Tightening the suspension helps prevent the diving but may have to do some more fine tuning to feel comfortable around high speed turns. After getting cofortable with the Fox Shocks we will be installing ORI Struts brand new bolt in struts specifically build for the RZR 1000 and Turbo XP models. Can't wait to feel the comparison.
